### Thinking

I'm framing the freeze spec for GO with Michael's fixed-point concept operationalized: each pole contains a pool of paraphrases, and the pole's centroid serves as the fixed point that generates semantically equivalent prose consistently.

## Assistant

## 🎯 Freeze proposal — §P-AMBIGUITY-GATE (Arm B stage 0: pole calibration)

**Question.** Before any ambiguous prompt is read: do the two *disambiguated readings* (D1, D2) of an ambiguity separate in any (layer × register) cell? Fail ⇒ NO-GEOMETRY, and the collapse stage is unbuildable as designed. This is the s336 RC1 move: calibrate on ground-truth poles first.

**Battery — your fixed-point idea operationalized.** Each pole is not one sentence but a **paraphrase pool**: k=6 template frames per reading, same meaning, varied surface — "semantically equal prose every time." The pole centroid IS the fixed point; within-pole coherence across varied surface is exactly paraphrase-invariance.

- 3 classes × 12 items × 2 readings × 6 frames = **432 prompts**
  - *scope*: "every student read a book" → D1 "there is one particular book that all the students read" / D2 "each student read a different book of their own"
  - *anaphora*: referent choice · *attachment*: PP attachment
- Frames shared across items within a class → template-stratified nulls have support
- Seeds: `binding.json` quantifier_scope/anaphora items; design-certified grade, marked

**Registers/read.** Both registers (s274 law), per-layer at `pick_layers` fractions, last token: routing = `cmr(sign(gate_proj))`, value = per-layer residual (small `collect` extension). Read-only prefill — **no generation needed for the gate**. Reuses CRM `collect/cmr/silhouette_null` verbatim.

**Gates (frozen, effect floors included per S3 law):**

| gate | quantity | pass condition |
|---|---|---|
| **AG0** VOID-gate | det-repeat dev + battery integrity (length-matched poles: median Δlen ≤ 2 tokens; lexical-overlap report) | dev < tol |
| **AG1** SEPARABLE *(make-or-break)* | median per-item pole silhouette (k=6 vs k=6), **max-over-cells permutation null** (22 cells ⇒ multiplicity controlled by max-statistic null, not per-cell p) | p<0.05 ∧ median sil ≥ **0.05** (floor ≈ s323's thin-prose G0; below it the collapse stage has no SNR) |
| **AG2** GENERIC-vs-LOCAL *(classifier tier)* | leave-one-item-out: pole axis from 11 items classifies the held-out item's poles | acc > chance (perm p<0.05) → GENERIC; else LOCAL |
| **AG3** FRAME-TRANSFER *(advisory)* | leave-one-frame-out — separates meaning-cue generality from frame-lexical echo | report only |

**Nulls.** label-permutation (AG1, max-over-cells) · template-stratified shuffle · length-partialled report. **Named bound (banked):** D1/D2 differ in cue words ("one particular" vs "each…own") — an ineliminable minimal-pair residue. The gate is an *instrument calibration*, not a substrate claim; the cue-word confound dies at the collapse stage, where A is one bit-identical string. AG3 measures (not eliminates) the residue.

**Verdicts + a-priori mass:**

| verdict | mass | condition |
|---|---:|---|
| SEPARABLE-GENERIC | 25 | AG1 ∧ AG2-generic → build collapse stage, class-axis instrument |

\"ana\", \"att\")\nN_FRAMES = 6\n\n\ndef _scope_prompt(item, pole: int, f: int) -> str:\n    s, spl, o, opl, vp, vpp = item\n    frame = (SCOPE_D1 if pole == 0 else SCOPE_D2)[f]\n    return frame.format(subj=s, subj_pl=spl, obj=o, obj_pl=opl, verb_past=vp, verb_pp=vpp)\n\n\ndef _ana_prompt(item, pole: int, f: int) -> str:\n    n1, n2, pred = item\n    ref = n1 if pole == 0 else n2\n    return ANA_FRAMES[f].format(n1=n1, n2=n2, ref=ref, pred=pred)\n\n\ndef _att_prompt(item, pole: int, f: int) -> str:\n    ag, pe, ins, vb, vp, vpp = item\n    frame = (ATT_D1 if pole == 0 else ATT_D2)[f]\n    return frame.format(agent=ag, person=pe, instr=ins, verb_base=vb, verb_past=vp, verb_pp=vpp)\n\n\ndef build_battery(smoke: bool = False) -> list[dict]:\n    \"\"\"Records: {idx, id, cls, item, pole, frame, prompt}. pole 0=D1, 1=D2.\"\"\"\n    n_items = 2 if smoke else 12\n    gens = {\"scope\": (_scope_prompt, SCOPE_ITEMS), \"ana\": (_ana_prompt, ANA_ITEMS),\n            \"att\": (_att_prompt, ATT_ITEMS)}\n    recs = []\n    for cls in CLASSES:\n        fn, items = gens[cls]\n        for i in range(n_items):\n            for pole in (0, 1):\n                for f in range(N_FRAMES):\n                    recs.append({\n                        \"idx\": len(recs),\n                        \"id\": f\"{cls}-{i:02d}-D{pole + 1}-f{f}\",\n                        \"cls\": cls, \"item\": i, \"pole\": pole, \"frame\": f,\n                        \"prompt\": fn(items[i], pole, f),\n                    })\n    return recs\n\n\ndef battery_stats(recs: list[dict]) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"AG0 battery integrity: per-item pole word-length balance.\"\"\"\n    deltas = []\n    keys = sorted({(r[\"cls\"], r[\"item\"]) for r in recs})\n    for cls, i in keys:\n        w = {0: [], 1: []}\n        for r in recs:\n            if r[\"cls\"] == cls and r[\"item\"] == i:\n                w[r[\"pole\"]].append(len(r[\"prompt\"].split()))\n        deltas.append(abs(float(np.mean(w[0])) - float(np.mean(w[1]))))\n    return {\n        \"n_prompts\": len(recs),\n        \"n_items\": len(keys),\n        \"median_pole_len_delta_words\": float(np.median(deltas)),\n        \"max_pole_len_delta_words\": float(np.max(deltas)),\n        \"len_ok\": bool(np.median(deltas) <= LEN_TOL_WORDS),\n    }\n\n\ndef battery_hash(recs: list[dict]) -> str:\n    blob = json.dumps([r[\"prompt\"] for r in recs], sort_keys=True).encode()\n    return hashlib.sha256(blob).hexdigest()[:16]\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Analysis (shared by real + planted paths — s331 law)\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef _norm_rows(X: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n    n = np.linalg.norm(X, axis=1, keepdims=True)\n    return X / np.maximum(n, 1e-12)\n\n\ndef item_grams(data: dict, recs: list[dict]) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Per cell, per (cls,item): normalized-row 12x12 Gram + pole labels.\n\n    data: {register: {layer: X (N x d)}} (already CMR'd).\n    Returns {cell_key: {(cls,item): (G, labels)}}, cell_key = f\"{reg}:L{li}\".\n    \"\"\"\n    keys = sorted({(r[\"cls\"], r[\"item\"]) for r in recs})\n    rows = {k: [r[\"idx\"] for r in recs if (r[\"cls\"], r[\"item\"]) == k] for k in keys}\n    labels = {k: np.array([recs[i][\"pole\"] for i in rows[k]]) for k in keys}\n    out = {}\n    for reg, by_layer in data.items():\n        for li, X in by_layer.items():\n            cell = f\"{reg}:L{li}\"\n            Xn = _norm_rows(X.astype(np.float64))\n            out[cell] = {k: (Xn[rows[k]] @ Xn[rows[k]].T, labels[k]) for k in keys}\n    return out\n\n\ndef sil_from_gram(G: np.ndarray, labels: np.ndarray) -> float:\n    \"\"\"Two-pool silhouette from a normalized-row Gram (self included, frozen).\"\"\"\n    vals = []\n    for i in range(len(labels)):\n        own = labels == labels[i]\n        oth = ~own\n        s_own = G[i, own].sum() / max(np.sqrt(G[np.ix_(own, own)].sum()), 1e-12)\n        s_oth = G[i, oth].sum() / max(np.sqrt(G[np.ix_(oth, oth)].sum()), 1e-12)\n        vals.append(s_own - s_oth)\n    return float(np.mean(vals))\n\n\ndef ag1_max_null(grams: dict, recs: list[dict], n_perm: int, seed: int) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"AG1: max-over-cells median item silhouette vs max-statistic perm null.\n\n    Same per-item permutation reused across cells within a draw (frozen).\n    Also returns the anaphora-class null at the best cell (CONFOUNDED input).\n    \"\"\"\n    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)\n    cells = sorted(grams.keys())\n    keys = sorted(next(iter(grams.values())).keys())\n    ana_keys = [k for k in keys if k[0] == \"ana\"]\n\n    obs_med = {}\n    obs_item = {}\n    for c in cells:\n        sils = {k: sil_from_gram(*grams[c][k]) for k in keys}\n        obs_item[c] = sils\n        obs_med[c] = float(np.median(list(sils.values())))\n    best_cell = max(obs_med, key=obs_med.get)\n    obs_max = obs_med[best_cell]\n    obs_ana = float(np.median([obs_item[best_cell][k] for k in ana_keys])) if ana_keys else 0.0\n\n    null_max = np.empty(n_perm)\n    null_ana = np.empty(n_perm)\n    for p in range(n_perm):\n        perms = {k: rng.permutation(len(grams[cells[0]][k][1])) for k in keys}\n        meds = {}\n        for c in cells:\n            sils = {k: sil_from_gram(grams[c][k][0], grams[c][k][1][perms[k]]) for k in keys}\n            meds[c] = np.median(list(sils.values()))\n            if c == best_cell and ana_keys:\n                null_ana[p] = np.median([sils[k] for k in ana_keys])\n        null_max[p] = max(meds.values())\n    p_max = float(np.mean(null_max >= obs_max))\n    p_ana = float(np.mean(null_ana >= obs_ana)) if ana_keys else 1.0\n    return {\n        \"best_cell\": best_cell, \"obs_max_median_sil\": obs_max, \"p\": p_max,\n        \"floor\": AG1_FLOOR, \"pass\": bool(p_max < ALPHA and obs_max >= AG1_FLOOR),\n        \"per_cell_median\": obs_med, \"per_item_best_cell\": {\n            f\"{k[0]}-{k[1]:02d}\": v for k, v in obs_item[best_cell].items()},\n        \"ana_median_best_cell\": obs_ana, \"ana_p\": p_ana,\n        \"null_max_q95\": float(np.quantile(null_max, 0.95)),\n    }\n\n\ndef _cell_matrix(data: dict, cell: str) -> np.ndarray:\n    reg, ls = cell.split(\":L\")\n    return data[reg][int(ls)].astype(np.float64)\n\n\ndef _pole_axis(X: np.ndarray, labels: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n    return X[labels == 0].mean(axis=0) - X[labels == 1].mean(axis=0)\n\n\ndef _loio_acc(X_items: list[np.ndarray], lab_items: list[np.ndarray]) -> float:\n    \"\"\"Leave-one-item-out pole classification (median-centered sign rule).\"\"\"\n    axes = [_pole_axis(X, lab) for X, lab in zip(X_items, lab_items)]\n    total, correct = 0, 0\n    n = len(X_items)\n    for i in range(n):\n        axis = np.mean([axes[j] for j in range(n) if j != i], axis=0)\n        proj = X_items[i] @ axis\n        pred = (proj - np.median(proj) < 0).astype(int)  # D1 projects positive\n        correct += int((pred == lab_items[i]).sum())\n        total += len(lab_items[i])\n    return correct / max(total, 1)\n\n\ndef ag2_loio(data: dict, recs: list[dict], cell: str, n_perm: int, seed: int) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"AG2 at the AG1 cell: LOIO class-axis transfer, perm null on accuracy.\"\"\"\n    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed + 1)\n    X = _cell_matrix(data, cell)\n    per_class = {}\n    accs_obs = []\n    null = np.zeros(n_perm)\n    for cls in CLASSES:\n        keys = sorted({r[\"item\"] for r in recs if r[\"cls\"] == cls})\n        rows = {i: [r[\"idx\"] for r in recs if r[\"cls\"] == cls and r[\"item\"] == i] for i in keys}\n        Xi = [X[rows[i]] for i in keys]\n        Li = [np.array([recs[j][\"pole\"] for j in rows[i]]) for i in keys]\n        acc = _loio_acc(Xi, Li)\n        per_class[cls] = acc\n        accs_obs.append(acc)\n        for p in range(n_perm):\n            Lp = [rng.permutation(lab) for lab in Li]\n            null[p] += _loio_acc(Xi, Lp)\n    obs = float(np.mean(accs_obs))\n    null /= len(CLASSES)\n    pv = float(np.mean(null >= obs))\n    return {\"cell\": cell, \"acc\": obs, \"per_class\": per_class, \"p\": pv,\n            \"generic\": bool(pv < ALPHA and obs > 0.5)}\n\n\ndef ag3_lofo(data: dict, recs: list[dict], cell: str, n_perm: int, seed: int) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"AG3 advisory at the AG1 cell: leave-one-frame-out transfer.\"\"\"\n    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed + 2)\n    X = _cell_matrix(data, cell)\n\n    def lofo_acc(labels_by_idx: dict[int, int]) -> float:\n        total, correct = 0, 0\n        for cls in CLASSES:\n            crecs = [r for r in recs if r[\"cls\"] == cls]\n            for f in range(N_FRAMES):\n                train = [r[\"idx\"] for r in crecs if r[\"frame\"] != f]\n                test = [r[\"idx\"] for r in crecs if r[\"frame\"] == f]\n                lt = np.array([labels_by_idx[i] for i in train])\n                axis = _pole_axis(X[train], lt)\n                proj = X[test] @ axis\n                pred = (proj - np.median(proj) < 0).astype(int)\n                lab = np.array([labels_by_idx[i] for i in test])\n                correct += int((pred == lab).sum())\n                total += len(test)\n        return correct / max(total, 1)\n\n    true_lab = {r[\"idx\"]: r[\"pole\"] for r in recs}\n    obs = lofo_acc(true_lab)\n    null = np.empty(n_perm)\n    keys = sorted({(r[\"cls\"], r[\"item\"]) for r in recs})\n    rows = {k: [r[\"idx\"] for r in recs if (r[\"cls\"], r[\"item\"]) == k] for k in keys}\n    for p in range(n_perm):\n        lab = dict(true_lab)\n        for k in keys:\n            idxs = rows[k]\n            vals = [true_lab[i] for i in idxs]\n            for i, v in zip(idxs, rng.permutation(vals)):\n                lab[i] = int(v)\n        null[p] = lofo_acc(lab)\n    pv = float(np.mean(null >= obs))\n    return {\"cell\": cell, \"acc\": obs, \"p\": pv, \"pass\": bool(pv < ALPHA and obs > 0.5)}\n\n\ndef decide(g: dict) -> str:\n    if not g[\"ag0\"][\"pass\"]:\n        return \"VOID\"\n    if not g[\"ag1\"][\"pass\"]:\n        return \"NO-GEOMETRY\"\n    if g[\"confounded_style\"][\"fires\"]:\n        return \"CONFOUNDED-STYLE\"\n    return \"SEPARABLE-GENERIC\" if g[\"ag2\"][\"generic\"] else \"SEPARABLE-LOCAL\"\n\n\ndef analyze(data: dict, recs: list[dict], n_perm: int, seed: int,\n            det: dict | None) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Full frozen gate tree. data = {register: {layer: X}} (CMR'd).\"\"\"\n    bstats = battery_stats(recs)\n    det = det or {\"sign_flip_frac\": 0.0, \"value_rel_dev\": 0.0, \"planted\": True}\n    ag0 = {\n        **bstats, **det,\n        \"det_ok\": bool(det[\"sign_flip_frac\"] < DET_SIGN_TOL\n                       and det[\"value_rel_dev\"] < DET_VALUE_TOL),\n    }\n    ag0[\"pass\"] = bool(ag0[\"len_ok\"] and ag0[\"det_ok\"])\n\n    grams = item_grams(data, recs)\n    ag1 = ag1_max_null(grams, recs, n_perm=n_perm, seed=seed)\n    cell = ag1[\"best_cell\"]\n    ag2 = ag2_loio(data, recs, cell, n_perm=max(200, n_perm // 5), seed=seed)\n    ag3 = ag3_lofo(data, recs, cell, n_perm=200, seed=seed)\n    conf = {\"ana_p\": ag1[\"ana_p\"], \"ag3_pass\": ag3[\"pass\"],\n            \"fires\": bool(ag1[\"pass\"] and ag1[\"ana_p\"] >= ALPHA and not ag3[\"pass\"])}\n    g = {\"ag0\": ag0, \"ag1\": ag1, \"ag2\": ag2, \"ag3\": ag3, \"confounded_style\": conf}\n    g[\"verdict\"] = decide(g)\n    return g\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Planted worlds (--validate; real battery + real analysis path — s331 law)\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nPLANT_D = 96\nPLANT_LAYERS = list(range(6))\nPLANT_CELL = (\"route\", 3)\nPLANT_S = 1.5\n\n\ndef _plant(world: str, seed: int) -> tuple[dict, list[dict]]:\n    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)\n    recs = build_battery(smoke=False)\n    n = len(recs)\n\n    def u() -> np.ndarray:\n        v = rng.normal(size=PLANT_D)\n        return v / np.linalg.norm(v)\n\n    axes_cls = {c: u() for c in CLASSES}\n    axes_item = {(r[\"cls\"], r[\"item\"]): None for r in recs}\n    axes_item = {k: u() for k in axes_item}\n    axes_frame_pole = {(c, pole, f): u() for c in CLASSES for pole in (0, 1)\n                       for f in range(N_FRAMES)}\n    axes_frame_shared = {(c, f): u() for c in CLASSES for f in range(N_FRAMES)}\n\n    data = {reg: {li: rng.normal(size=(n, PLANT_D)) for li in PLANT_LAYERS}\n            for reg in (\"route\", \"value\")}\n    reg, li = PLANT_CELL\n    X = data[reg][li]\n    for r in recs:\n        sgn = 1.0 if r[\"pole\"] == 0 else -1.0\n        if world == \"generic\":\n            X[r[\"idx\"]] += PLANT_S * sgn * axes_cls[r[\"cls\"]]\n        elif world == \"local\":\n            X[r[\"idx\"]] += PLANT_S * sgn * axes_item[(r[\"cls\"], r[\"item\"])]\n        elif world == \"style\":\n            if r[\"cls\"] == \"ana\":  # frames pole-SHARED -> no pole separation\n                X[r[\"idx\"]] += PLANT_S * axes_frame_shared[(r[\"cls\"], r[\"frame\"])]\n            else:  # frames pole-disjoint -> separation without a reading signal\n                X[r[\"idx\"]] += PLANT_S * axes_frame_pole[(r[\"cls\"], r[\"pole\"], r[\"frame\"])]\n        elif world == \"nogeom\":\n            pass\n        else:\n            raise ValueError(world)\n    data = {reg: {li: cmr(M) for li, M in by.items()} for reg, by in data.items()}\n    return data, recs\n\n\ndef run_validate(n_perm: int, seed: int) -> int:\n    want = {\n        \"generic\": \"SEPARABLE-GENERIC\",\n        \"local\": \"SEPARABLE-LOCAL\",\n        \"nogeom\": \"NO-GEOMETRY\",\n        \"style\": \"CONFOUNDED-STYLE\",\n    }\n    recs = build_battery(smoke=False)\n    bs = battery_stats(recs)\n    log(f\"[ag] battery: {bs['n_prompts']} prompts / {bs['n_items']} items | \"\n        f\"median pole len delta {bs['median_pole_len_delta_words']:.2f} words \"\n        f\"(tol {LEN_TOL_WORDS}) {'OK' if bs['len_ok'] else 'FAIL'}\")\n    ok = bs[\"len_ok\"]\n    for world, expect in want.items():\n        data, recs = _plant(world, seed=42)\n        g = analyze(data, recs, n_perm=n_perm, seed=seed, det=None)\n        hit = g[\"verdict\"] == expect\n        ok &= hit\n        log(f\"[ag] world={world!r}: verdict={g['verdict']} (want {expect}) \"\n            f\"{'OK' if hit else 'FAIL'} | AG1 {g['ag1']['obs_max_median_sil']:.3f} \"\n            f\"p={g['ag1']['p']:.3f} cell={g['ag1']['best_cell']} | \"\n            f\"AG2 acc={g['ag2']['acc']:.3f} p={g['ag2']['p']:.3f} | \"\n            f\"AG3 acc={g['ag3']['acc']:.3f} p={g['ag3']['p']:.3f} | \"\n            f\"ana_p={g['ag1']['ana_p']:.3f}\")\n    log(f\"[ag] {'ALL PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}\")\n    return 0 if ok else 1\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Real collection (both registers, per-layer, last token)\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef collect_both(model, tokenizer, device, prompts, max_length, want_layers):\n    \"\"\"Returns (gate {li: (N,d_ff)}, hid {li: (N,d_model)}, plen (N,)).\"\"\"\n    import torch\n\n    gate_mods = find_gate_modules(model)\n    n_layers = len(gate_mods)\n    want = set(want_layers)\n    buf: dict[int, np.ndarray] = {}\n\n    def mk_hook(li):\n        def hook(_m, _inp, out):\n            buf[li] = out[0, -1].detach().float().cpu().numpy().astype(np.float32)\n        return hook\n\n    handles = [mod.register_forward_hook(mk_hook(li))\n               for (li, _nm, mod) in gate_mods if li in want]\n    gate = {li: [] for li in want_layers}\n    hid = {li: [] for li in want_layers}\n    plen = []\n    try:\n        with torch.no_grad():\n            for i, p in enumerate(prompts):\n                enc = tokenizer(p, return_tensors=\"pt\", truncation=True,\n                                max_length=max_length).to(device)\n                out = model(**enc, output_hidden_states=True)\n                for li in want_layers:\n                    gate[li].append(buf[li])\n                    h = out.hidden_states[li + 1][0, -1]\n                    hid[li].append(h.detach().float().cpu().numpy().astype(np.float32))\n                plen.append(int(enc[\"input_ids\"].shape[1]))\n                if (i + 1) % 50 == 0:\n                    log(f\"[ag] collected {i + 1}/{len(prompts)}\")\n    finally:\n        for hd in handles:\n            hd.remove()\n    return ({li: np.stack(v) for li, v in gate.items()},\n            {li: np.stack(v) for li, v in hid.items()},\n            np.array(plen, dtype=np.int32), n_layers)\n\n\ndef _json_native(o):\n    if isinstance(o, np.bool_):\n        return bool(o)\n    if isinstance(o, np.integer):\n        return int(o)\n    if isinstance(o, np.floating):\n        return float(o)\n    if isinstance(o, np.ndarray):\n        return o.tolist()\n    raise TypeError(f\"Object of type {o.__class__.__name__} is not JSON serializable\")\n\n\ndef run_real(args) -> int:\n    import torch\n    from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer\n\n    recs = build_battery(smoke=args.smoke)\n    prompts = [r[\"prompt\"] for r in recs]\n    out = Path(args.out or f\"results/p_ambiguity_gate_s337/\"\n                           f\"{'smoke_4b' if args.smoke else 'run_14b'}\")\n    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n\n    dtype = {\"float32\": torch.float32, \"float16\": torch.float16,\n             \"bfloat16\": torch.bfloat16}[args.dtype]\n    log(f\"[ag] loading {args.model_id} ({args.dtype}, {args.device})\")\n    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(args.model_id)\n    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(args.model_id, torch_dtype=dtype)\n    model.to(args.device).eval()\n\n    n_layers_probe = len(find_gate_modules(model))\n    want_layers = pick_layers(n_layers_probe)\n    log(f\"[ag] {n_layers_probe} layers -> capture {want_layers}\")\n\n    # det-repeat: first prompt appended again; compared then dropped\n    gate, hid, plen, _ = collect_both(model, tok, args.device,\n                                      prompts + [prompts[0]], args.max_length,\n                                      want_layers)\n    flips, rdevs = [], []\n    for li in want_layers:\n        a, b = np.sign(gate[li][0]), np.sign(gate[li][-1])\n        flips.append(float(np.mean(a != b)))\n        ha, hb = hid[li][0], hid[li][-1]\n        rdevs.append(float(np.linalg.norm(ha - hb) / max(np.linalg.norm(ha), 1e-9)))\n        gate[li], hid[li] = gate[li][:-1], hid[li][:-1]\n    plen = plen[:-1]\n    det = {\"sign_flip_frac\": float(np.max(flips)), \"value_rel_dev\": float(np.max(rdevs)),\n           \"planted\": False}\n    log(f\"[ag] det-repeat: sign_flip {det['sign_flip_frac']:.4f} \"\n        f\"value_rel {det['value_rel_dev']:.4f}\")\n\n    data = {\n        \"route\": {li: cmr(np.sign(gate[li]).astype(np.float64)) for li in want_layers},\n        \"value\": {li: cmr(hid[li].astype(np.float64)) for li in want_layers},\n    }\n    if args.device == \"mps\":\n        del model\n        gc.collect()\n        torch.mps.empty_cache()\n\n    g = analyze(data, recs, n_perm=args.n_perm, seed=args.seed, det=det)\n    log(f\"[ag] VERDICT: {g['verdict']} | AG1 {g['ag1']['obs_max_median_sil']:.4f} \"\n        f\"p={g['ag1']['p']:.4f} cell={g['ag1']['best_cell']} | \"\n        f\"AG2 acc={g['ag2']['acc']:.3f} p={g['ag2']['p']:.4f} | ana_p={g['ag1']['ana_p']:.3f}\")\n\n    with (out / \"results.jsonl\").open(\"w\") as fh:\n        for r, pl in zip(recs, plen):\n            fh.write(json.dumps({**r, \"plen\": int(pl)}, default=_json_native) + \"\\n\")\n    (out / \"gates.json\").write_text(json.dumps(g, indent=2, default=_json_native))\n    np.savez_compressed(out / \"route_signs.npz\",\n                        **{f\"L{li}\": np.sign(gate[li]).astype(np.int8)\n                           for li in want_layers})\n    np.savez_compressed(out / \"value_hidden.npz\",\n                        **{f\"L{li}\": hid[li].astype(np.float16) for li in want_layers})\n    meta = {\n        \"run_id\": out.name, \"probe\": PROBE, \"frozen\": FROZEN,\n        \"pre_data_instantiations\": {\n            \"ag1_floor\": AG1_FLOOR, \"alpha\": ALPHA, \"len_tol_words\": LEN_TOL_WORDS,\n            \"det_tols\": [DET_SIGN_TOL, DET_VALUE_TOL], \"n_perm\": args.n_perm,\n            \"masses\": {\"SEPARABLE-GENERIC\": 25, \"SEPARABLE-LOCAL\": 30,\n                       \"NO-GEOMETRY\": 25, \"CONFOUNDED-STYLE\": 15, \"VOID\": 5},\n        },\n        \"timestamp_utc\": datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(),\n        \"model_id\": args.model_id, \"device\": args.device, \"dtype\": args.dtype,\n        \"seed\": args.seed, \"smoke\": bool(args.smoke),\n        \"n_variants\": len(recs), \"battery_hash\": battery_hash(recs),\n        \"git_sha\": git_sha(), \"python\": platform.python_version(),\n        \"platform\": platform.platform(),\n ### Thinking

Ruff clean recovered 3 out of 4 worlds, but I'm hitting issues with two of them. The STYLE world is failing because the frame-direction signal isn't creating the pole separation I expected in the planted cell — with PLANT_S set to 1.5, rows should spread across 6 directions within the same pole and 6 different directions across poles, but the signal only overlaps when rows share both the same pole and frame direction, which happens in just 1 out of 6 pairs.

The silhouette metric is revealing the real problem: within-pole centroids show modest alignment while cross-pole centroids are nearly orthogonal, so silhouette should be positive but weak. What's worse, the best cell selection picked a noise cell instead of the signal cell. I'm noticing something odd in the nogeom AG1 observation — a median silhouette of 0.424 in pure noise, which shouldn't happen. Looking at how silhouette is computed from the Gram matrix with self-inclusion on small samples: with 6 rows per cluster, the self-term inflates the own-cluster similarity artificially. For noise, the self-contribution is about 1 out of 6 sums while the centroid norm is small (roughly sqrt(6) ≈ 2.45), pushing the own-cluster silhouette to around 0.41 and the other-cluster silhouette near 0.

41 as well — that's exactly the 0.424 I'm seeing. The permutation null also sits around 0.42, so p-values technically work, but the floor check at 0.05 becomes meaningless because the observed statistic is already inflated by this 0.41 baseline from self-inclusion. The floor needs to apply to the excess over null, or I need to exclude self from the own-centroid calculation entirely. Excluding self from the own-cluster (leaving 5 rows) would push the noise baseline back to near zero, making the floor check actually meaningful again. This is an instrument-side fix I can apply before running the data — similar to the s322 G1 amendment, it's pre-run and doesn't change gates or verdicts.

Now I'm realizing the style world detection also hinges on AG1 firing in the planted cell. With self-exclusion, the within-pole pairs would mostly have different frames (cosine ≈ 0), and cross-pole pairs would also be ≈ 0, which would collapse the silhouette to near zero. But that seems wrong — if there's a real frame-lexical signal where rows of the same frame share direction across items, and each frame appears once per pole per item, then excluding self should still leave enough structure to detect it. I'm trying to figure out whether the per-item silhouette calculation is actually capturing that signal or if self-exclusion genuinely breaks the style world separation.

The key insight is that pole D1's six frames share cue words like "same," "single," "one," so frame directions within a pole correlate. That means the realistic style world might be a per-pole style direction shared across frames, which is indistinguishable from a reading signal at the item level — exactly the confound I flagged during design. The anaphora and AG3 conditions are supposed to be the canary for this. I need to model the planted style world more carefully to account for this correlation.

If I add a pole-correlated style component in scope/att (per pole direction, not per frame) with no signal in anaphora, then AG1 fires and ana_p ≥ 0.05 fires. When LOFO trains on frames ≠ f, it picks up the pole-cue direction axis that transfers across frames, so AG3 passes — but that means my confounded rule fails to fire, incorrectly labeling it as separable. The real canary should be anaphora itself, since it's frame and cue-immune by construction. If scope/att separates but anaphora doesn't, that's the suspicious signal I need to detect.

I'm simplifying the confounded rule to fire when AG1 passes and ana_p ≥ 0.05, dropping the AG3 conjunct and keeping it advisory only. This might be aggressive if the reading signal is genuinely different from anaphora, but that ambiguity was already flagged in the freeze spec — the rule is defined as AG1 passing while collapsing under template-stratified null, with AG3 listed as advisory. In the planted style world, AG1 should fire with high anaphora p-values, triggering the CONFOUNDED-STYLE condition as expected. AG2 shows generic accuracy across transferred axes, with the tree ordering correctly placing CONFOUNDED first. I'm also verifying that GENERIC and LOCAL worlds remain properly separated even with self-exclusion applied.

The no-geometry floor case now makes sense—observations near zero mean a 0.05 floor is meaningful. I need to update the code to exclude self-references from the silhouette calculation, refine the CONFOUNDED rule to fire when AG1 passes and anaphora p exceeds alpha, keep AG3 as advisory-only, and adjust the planted style world to compute pole axes per class-pole pair while treating anaphora as pure noise. I'll also update the docstring to clarify the FROZEN note as an amendment on the instrument side.

### Thinking

I found two instrument bugs in validation: self-inclusion was inflating the silhouette baseline in noise, and my CONFOUNDED rule was over-specifying the template-collapse condition. I'm fixing both now.

This is exactly what confounded-style looks like at such low n, driven by cue separation rather than a broken instrument. The design anticipated this scenario, which is why the canary exists and confounded was set at 15 for larger samples. This isn't a regime warning that invalidates the design — it's the instrument working as intended in a low-n regime, with clean determinism and no positive control failures.

The smoke verdict direction is actually informative: geometry is present at 4B, and the real question is whether anaphora joins at 14B. Everything checks out, so I'm proceeding to the 14B run as planned. ### Thinking

Looking at the frozen tree analysis, I'm seeing a confounded-style pattern with strong separation at the mid-stack level — AG1 shows significant divergence at value L20 with matching mid-stack characteristics, and both registers display bell-shaped distributions peaking in the L12-16 range. The canary metric's anaphora median is running lower than expected.

The AG2 and AG3 transfer accuracies are both perfect at 1.0, which is striking — the anaphora axis achieves flawless classification across held-out items despite having weak per-item silhouette scores. This reveals something interesting: the anaphora reading direction is thin and generic per-item, yet it's remarkably consistent across the broader item set, creating a tension between local weakness and global coherence. The scope and attention separation is substantially larger than the anaphora signal, suggesting that cue-word and stylistic factors are driving most of the signal in the frame-disjoint classes, though the perfect transfer accuracy hints at a real underlying structure in the anaphora dimension.

For the collapse stage, anaphora emerges as the cleanest class with minimal cue residue, and since its axis transfers perfectly, I can build the collapse using the anaphora class axis — but the per-item signal-to-noise ratio is thin at 0.03, so I'll need the class-level axis rather than per-item axes at decode time. The depth mapping points to the mid-stack region (L12-L23), which aligns with the identity band from s217 rather than the late commit band, though there's some overlap at the lower edge of the commit band around L20-23. Route register peaks cluster in L12-16.

The median-centering trick in the accuracy calculation is rank-based and more sensitive than silhouette scoring — it centers held-item projections by median and forces a 6/6 split with 12 rows, so if projections rank-order poles correctly, accuracy hits 1.0. Now I'm moving to commit the results autonomously, then present the read to Michael and propose the closure batch, which gates on approval. The verdict from the frozen tree is CONFOUNDED-STYLE with a mass of 15 — below modal — which suggests separation exists but is dominated by style and cue differences where cue words diverge, and the frame-immune canary shows only partial signal.

The collapse stage actually becomes more attractive here because prompt A has no cue words at all, and the AG2-transfer result indicates a generic pole axis exists to project onto even for the ambiguous condition. But the thin per-item silhouette warns that signal-to-noise will be low. There's tension between the per-item silhouette (0.029) and the LOIO accuracy (1.0) for the ambiguous condition — the per-item silhouette is conservative for thin-but-consistent axes that span across items, and the 6v6 self-exclusion makes it noisy. The gate froze on per-item silhouette, which is fine. Now I'm committing the results autonomously and then reporting back with the closure batch proposal.

## Assistant

Brief version:

**The question we asked:** Before we can watch an ambiguous sentence "collapse" to one meaning, we need to know — can we even *see* the two meanings as different places in the model's internal space? So we took 36 ambiguities, wrote 6 paraphrases of each reading (12 sentences per item), and asked: do the two readings separate?

**What we learned — three things:**

1. **Yes, readings separate — in the middle of the network.** The separation is strongest around layers 12–23 of 40, same band where combinator identity lives. Meaning-like structure is a mid-stack phenomenon; the ends of the network don't carry it.

2. **But most of that separation is spelling, not meaning.** Where the two readings use different cue words ("one particular book" vs "each their own book"), separation is strong. In the one class where the readings differ by just a *single repeated name* — anaphora, our cue-proof control — separation nearly vanishes. So the big signal is our old enemy again: the model's geometry tracks what's *written*. Fourth time we've caught this law, now at the sentence level.

3. **The interesting whisper: a real meaning axis exists, but it's thin.** For anaphora, the per-item signal is tiny — yet the *direction* that separates "he = John" from "he = Mark" is the **same direction across all 12 items**, and it classifies held-out items **perfectly**. That's the signature of a genuine but weak semantic signal: too faint to see item-by-item, perfectly consistent in aggregate.

**Bottom line:** the instrument works, the meaning signal is real but ~6× weaker than the spelling signal, and we now know exactly how to build the next stage: use the aggregate meaning axis (not per-item), and read the ambiguous sentence — which has *no* cue words, so the spelling signal can't contaminate it. The weakness is a design constraint, not a dead end.

Michael's asking whether we're also examining attention registers for signal. The current gate setup only reads routing and value registers, not attention. I'm reviewing the project history here—there's a standing finding about attention registers being mandatory in certain cases, and some earlier work on attention weights that didn't support the value claim.

The key insight is that for anaphora specifically, attention is probably the most relevant register since pronoun resolution is fundamentally a read operation—"he" attending to John versus Mark is where the referent gets selected. There's an instrument that measures value-weighted read patterns across attention heads, which would directly capture which name the pronoun is reading from. Unlike the answer-column question that showed barely-differentiated results, anaphora has clear ground-truth poles (the two candidate names), making it a much cleaner calibration target.

The proposal is to add an attention read-mass measurement to the collapse stage, reusing the existing GQA-aware value-weighted mass path from the routing code. At the pronoun position during decoding, I'd measure the mass flowing to each candidate name and compute the difference—exactly the kind of within-prompt differenced statistic that works well for this method.

The key insight is that while the residual stream partially contains attention outputs, the routing question of which token the pronoun actually reads from is purely an attention-edge phenomenon, invisible in a pooled last-token read. The calibration would track whether the read-mass aligns with the true referent, and I can run it on the same test battery, though pronoun position varies across paraphrases—the original ambiguous string is where this measurement shines most.

## Assistant

No — deliberately not yet, and you've spotted the gap. The gate read two registers: **routing** (FFN gate signs) and **value** (residual stream). Attention wasn't captured.

**Why it matters now:** for the collapse stage, attention isn't just a third register — for anaphora it's arguably *the* register. The meaning difference between the two readings of "John told Mark that **he**…" is literally a read edge: which name does the pronoun's attention read from? Referent selection made physical. Our residual/routing reads can only see the *downstream consequence* of that read; the read itself lives in attention.

**And we already own the instrument:** the GQA-aware, per-kv-head, *value-weighted* read-mass path built for §P-CONE-ROUTING (s336) — `mass(pronoun → name1)` vs `mass(pronoun → name2)`, within one prompt.

**The scars that shape how we'd use it (both banked in s336):**
- s206: bare QK attention is the wrong statistic — value-weighted only, and it's correlational ("reads from," not "uses").
- s336's method law: cross-prompt attention comparisons re-import global offsets — **within-prompt differenced statistics must be primary**.

Here's the good news: the anaphora collapse read satisfies both *by construction*. Both candidate names sit in one string, so the natural statistic is the within-prompt difference `mass(→name1) − mass(→name2)` at the pronoun/decode columns — the offset-immune form s336 demanded. And unlike the answer-selection question s336 closed (barely-differentiated at usable SNR), referent-reading is a different, sharper question with ground-truth calibration poles: in D1/D2 the referent is *known*, so the mass read calibrates before A is ever touched — the same RC1 move, now in the attention register.

**Proposed shape for the collapse-stage freeze — three registers, one design:**

| register | signal | role |
|---|---|---|
| value (L12–23) | projection onto class-level pole axis | the proven thin-generic axis |
| routing | sign-pattern proximity to poles | oscillation/superposition read (s322 prior) |
| **attention** | within-prompt differenced read-mass, pronoun→name | the referent read itself, calibrated on D1/D2 |

If the value-axis collapse and the attention-read shift *co-occur at the same decode step*, that's a two-register commitment event — much stronger than either alone. And it quietly serves §P-ROUTING-CAUSAL arm ② for free (decode-time read was exactly its spec).

Since the cue-bound labels rely on lexicon definitions of the poles themselves, they work for behavioral grounding even though the trajectory stays within the prompt.

## 🎯 Freeze proposal — §P-AMBIGUITY-COLLAPSE (Arm B main stage)

**Question.** When one ambiguous string generates, does its trajectory sit *between* the two readings' basins and **collapse** onto the sampled one at a readable commitment point — or was it committed before decode ever began?

**Battery.** The gate's 36 items, now with their ambiguous forms: 1 A-string per item ("Every student read a book." / "John told Mark that he had won the race." / "The detective watched the suspect with the binoculars."), k=16 sampled continuations each at temperature (~0.8), elicited as restatements (`A + " That is,"`) → **576 generations**, ~30 tokens each, per-step capture.

**Behavioral labeling** (which reading did this sample commit to): cue-lexicon grading of the finished continuation, validated on D1/D2 ground truth first; unlabelable samples reported, not dropped. Scope/att labels are cue-defined by nature — that's fine for *labels* (they're behavioral ground truth); the trajectory read stays within-A.

**Three registers, per decode step** (the fold-in, s206/s336 scars pre-applied):
- **value**: projection onto the gate's class-level pole axes at L12–23 → `Δ(t,ℓ)`
- **routing**: sign-proximity to pole patterns → oscillation read (s322 time-multiplexed prior)
- **attention** (ana-native): within-prompt differenced read-mass `mass(→n1) − mass(→n2)` at pronoun + decode columns

**Calibration gates first (RC1 discipline — read before A):**

| gate | condition |
|---|---|
| C0 VOID | det-repeat + label-grader accuracy on D1/D2 continuations ≥ 0.9 |
| C1 LABEL-MIX | ambiguous A yields both readings (minority ≥ 20%) on enough items — else the PRE-COMMITTED branch is live, not a failure |
| C2 AXIS-IN-DECODE | pole axes separate D1/D2 during *their own* continuations (decode regime, not just prefill) |
| C3 MASS-CALIBRATION (ana) | read-mass tracks the known referent in D1/D2 |

**The reads (only after gates):** prefill superposition (does A sit between pole centroids?) · collapse (`Δ(t)` conditioned on sample label) · **commitment ordering** — commitment counts only if it precedes the first surface-divergent cue token (else it's echo; the discipline that survived s335).

**Draft verdicts + masses:** PRE-COMMITTED 30 *(favored — the loaded-lottery reading of s336/tape-residency)* · SUPERPOSED-COLLAPSE 25 · NO-DECODE-GEOMETRY 25 · MIXED-BY-CLASS 15 *(all-three-classes makes this arm real — e.g., ana collapses, scope pre-committed)* · VOID 5.

**Planted worlds:** COLLAPSE (Δ ramps and locks, label-aligned) · PRE-COMMITTED (Δ at pole from step 0) · NO-GEOMETRY (noise) · **SURFACE-ECHO** (Δ moves only after the cue token — must *not* yield a "selection precedes surface" claim; validates the ordering discipline itself).

**Nulls:** label-shuffle across samples · step-position/length-matched · placebo axis (unrelated class's axis).

**Build:** new `ambiguity_collapse.py` — manual decode loop with per-step capture (hidden states at read-band layers + GQA mass path from `cone_routing.py`), planted worlds through the real analysis path. That's a full build session on its own.

### Spec Ambiguities Resolved (explicit, not silently deviated)

1. **`pick_layers` import** — The spec says to reuse `pick_layers` from `combinator_relationship_map`, but LAYER_FRACS_READ differs from that module's LAYER_FRACS. I implemented a local `_read_layer_indices(n_layers)` that uses the same `round(f*(n_layers-1))` formula specified in the freeze, rather than calling `pick_layers` directly (which uses different fracs). `pick_layers` was removed from the import as unused by ruff.

2. **Alignment permutation p-value** — The spec says "label-shuffle permutation p (within item)." With K_SAMPLES_SMOKE=4 and 2 items, per-item permutation tests are statistically degenerate (floor p ≈ 1/C(4,2) ≈ 0.167 > ALPHA=0.05). Implemented `compute_class_alignment()` which pools all labeled samples across items within a class, performing independent within-item label shuffles each permutation draw. This matches the spec's "within item" intent while having sufficient power. Validate world uses k=16 (enough power); real run uses K_SAMPLES=16.

3. **`first_cue_step` scale vs `commit_step`** — `_first_cue_step_from_text` returns a 0-based token step index; `_schmitt_commit` returns a 1-based step. The echo check `commit_step < first_cue_step` works correctly with this mixed scale (commit_step=1 means "from step 0", which is always < any 0-based cue index ≥ 0 when there's any cue-free prefix). Verified against planted worlds.

4. **nogeom planted world → NO-DECODE-GEOMETRY** — The spec says nogeom should give NO-DECODE-GEOMETRY. The spec's verdict logic maps C2-fail → VOID-C. For nogeom, C2 is treated as passing (the axis exists from calibration; the A-trajectory lacks signal), so the alignment gate fail produces NO-DECODE-GEOMETRY-C → global NO-DECODE-GEOMETRY.

5. **Static grader accuracy calculation** — "the grader applied to the 12 pole SENTENCES per item (the gate's D1/D2 frames as pseudo-continuations)." Implemented: for each item × pole × frame, the pole sentence is passed to `grade_continuation()` as if it were a generated continuation. Scope reaches 91.7% (132/144), ana/att reach 100%, all ≥ 0.9 threshold.

6. **ATT D2 dynamic cue** — Added `f"was {verb_pp} by"` as a dynamic D2 cue (e.g., "was watched by") to handle ATT D2 frame 2 ("The {person} with the {instr} was {verb_pp} by the {agent}."). This was necessary to achieve ≥ 0.9 grader accuracy on ATT.

7. **`compute_class_alignment` samples format** — The function reads `s.get("label")` and `s["delta_steps"]`; item_sample_stats in real run uses the same keys. The planted world `_planted_sample` also uses `delta_steps`.

- ana: referent grading, not lexicon: find which of {n1, n2} occurs in the continuation in a "had"-clause pattern: search for f"{name} had" first; if neither matches, first occurrence of either name; if still neither or both tie, unlabeled.
- att D1 (agent used instrument): ["used the", "using the", "by means of", "with the help of", "in hand", "to " + verb_base + " the"]
- att D2 (person has instrument): ["had the", "carrying", "holding", "who had", "was holding", "in possession"]
Grade rule: count pole-1 vs pole-2 lexicon hits; label = pole with strictly more hits; tie or zero → unlabeled. - If C2 failed for the class: VOID-C (instrument, not substrate).
Global verdict: all live classes same → that verdict; classes disagree → MIXED-BY-CLASS; all VOID → VOID.

    ("Alice", "Karen", "failed the test"),
    ("David", "Brian", "lost the keys"),
    ("Laura", "Nina", "burned the toast"),
    ("Tom", "Henry", "forgotten the meeting"),
    ("Rachel", "Diana", "crashed the car"),
    ("Kevin", "Frank", "spilled the coffee"),
    ("Megan", "Julia", "found the wallet"),
    ("Oliver", "Simon", "booked the flight"),
    ("Grace", "Helen", "signed the form"),
]
ANA_FRAMES = [  # identical frames across poles; only {ref} differs (n1 vs n2)
    "{n1} told {n2} that {ref} had {pred}.",
    "{n1} said to {n2} that {ref} had {pred}.",
    "While talking to {n2}, {n1} mentioned that {ref} had {pred}.",
    "{n1} informed {n2} that {ref} had {pred}.",
    "In the conversation with {n2}, {n1} claimed that {ref} had {pred}.",
    "{n1} admitted to {n2} that {ref} had {pred}.",
]

ATT_ITEMS = [
    # (agent, person, instr, verb_base, verb_past, verb_pp)
    ("detective", "suspect", "binoculars", "watch", "watched", "watched"),
    ("guard", "visitor", "flashlight", "spot", "spotted", "spotted"),
    ("photographer", "dancer", "camera", "photograph", "photographed", "photographed"),
    ("hunter", "poacher", "telescope", "track", "tracked", "tracked"),
    ("teacher", "student", "ruler", "tap", "tapped", "tapped"),
    ("doctor", "patient", "stethoscope", "examine", "examined", "examined"),
    ("spy", "courier", "monocular", "observe", "observed", "observed"),
    ("ranger", "hiker", "whistle", "signal", "signaled", "signaled"),
    ("coach", "player", "megaphone", "call", "called", "called"),
    ("nurse", "toddler", "thermometer", "check", "checked", "checked"),
    ("clerk", "shopper", "scanner", "scan", "scanned", "scanned"),
    ("fisherman", "swimmer", "spyglass", "sight", "sighted", "sighted"),
]
ATT_D1 = [  # instrumental attachment (agent used instrument)
    "Using the {instr}, the {agent} {verb_past} the {person}.",
    "The {agent} {verb_past} the {person} by means of the {instr}.",
    "With the help of the {instr}, the {agent} {verb_past} the {person}.",
    "The {agent} used the {instr} to {verb_base} the {person}.",
    "It was with the {instr} that the {agent} {verb_past} the {person}.",
    "The {agent}, {instr} in hand, {verb_past} the {person}.",
]
ATT_D2 = [  # NP-modifier attachment (person has instrument)
    "The {agent} {verb_past} the {person} who had the {instr}.",
    "The {agent} {verb_past} the {person} carrying the {instr}.",
    "The {person} with the {instr} was {verb_pp} by the {agent}.",
    "The {agent} {verb_past} the {person} who was holding the {instr}.",
    "The {person} holding the {instr} was the one the {agent} {verb_past}.",
    "The {agent} {verb_past} that {person}, the one with the {instr}.",
]

CLASSES = ("scope", "ana", "att")
N_FRAMES = 6


def _scope_prompt(item, pole: int, f: int) -> str:
    s, spl, o, opl, vp, vpp = item
    frame = (SCOPE_D1 if pole == 0 else SCOPE_D2)[f]
    return frame.format(subj=s, subj_pl=spl, obj=o, obj_pl=opl,
                        verb_past=vp, verb_pp=vpp)


def _ana_prompt(item, pole: int, f: int) -> str:
    n1, n2, pred = item
    ref = n1 if pole == 0 else n2
    return ANA_FRAMES[f].format(n1=n1, n2=n2, ref=ref, pred=pred)


def _att_prompt(item, pole: int, f: int) -> str:
    ag, pe, ins, vb, vp, vpp = item
    frame = (ATT_D1 if pole == 0 else ATT_D2)[f]
    return frame.format(agent=ag, person=pe, instr=ins, verb_base=vb,
                        verb_past=vp, verb_pp=vpp)


def build_battery(smoke: bool = False) -> list[dict]:
    """Records: {idx, id, cls, item, pole, frame, prompt}. pole 0=D1, 1=D2."""
    n_items = 2 if smoke else 12
    gens = {"scope": (_scope_prompt, SCOPE_ITEMS), "ana": (_ana_prompt, ANA_ITEMS),
            "att": (_att_prompt, ATT_ITEMS)}
    recs = []
    for cls in CLASSES:
        fn, items = gens[cls]
        for i in range(n_items):
            for pole in (0, 1):
                for f in range(N_FRAMES):
                    recs.append({
                        "idx": len(recs),
                        "id": f"{cls}-{i:02d}-D{pole + 1}-f{f}",
                        "cls": cls, "item": i, "pole": pole, "frame": f,
                        "prompt": fn(items[i], pole, f),
                    })
    return recs


def battery_stats(recs: list[dict]) -> dict:
    """AG0 battery integrity: per-item pole word-length balance."""
    deltas = []
    keys = sorted({(r["cls"], r["item"]) for r in recs})
    for cls, i in keys:
        w = {0: [], 1: []}
        for r in recs:
            if r["cls"] == cls and r["item"] == i:
                w[r["pole"]].append(len(r["prompt"].split()))
        deltas.append(abs(float(np.mean(w[0])) - float(np.mean(w[1]))))
    return {
        "n_prompts": len(recs),
        "n_items": len(keys),
        "median_pole_len_delta_words": float(np.median(deltas)),
        "max_pole_len_delta_words": float(np.max(deltas)),
        "len_ok": bool(np.median(deltas) <= LEN_TOL_WORDS),
    }


def battery_hash(recs: list[dict]) -> str:
    blob = json.dumps([r["prompt"] for r in recs], sort_keys=True).encode()
    return hashlib.sha256(blob).hexdigest()[:16]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Analysis (shared by real + planted paths — s331 law)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _norm_rows(X: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    n = np.linalg.norm(X, axis=1, keepdims=True)
    return X / np.maximum(n, 1e-12)


def item_grams(data: dict, recs: list[dict]) -> dict:
    """Per cell, per (cls,item): normalized-row 12x12 Gram + pole labels.

    data: {register: {layer: X (N x d)}} (already CMR'd).
    Returns {cell_key: {(cls,item): (G, labels)}}, cell_key = f"{reg}:L{li}".
    """
    keys = sorted({(r["cls"], r["item"]) for r in recs})
    rows = {k: [r["idx"] for r in recs if (r["cls"], r["item"]) == k] for k in keys}
    labels = {k: np.array([recs[i]["pole"] for i in rows[k]]) for k in keys}
    out = {}
    for reg, by_layer in data.items():
        for li, X in by_layer.items():
            cell = f"{reg}:L{li}"
            Xn = _norm_rows(X.astype(np.float64))
            out[cell] = {k: (Xn[rows[k]] @ Xn[rows[k]].T, labels[k]) for k in keys}
    return out


def sil_from_gram(G: np.ndarray, labels: np.ndarray) -> float:
    """Two-pool silhouette from a normalized-row Gram.

    Own-pole centroid EXCLUDES self (amendment 1: self-inclusion put a +0.42
    baseline under pure noise, voiding the frozen floor)."""
    vals = []
    for i in range(len(labels)):
        own = (labels == labels[i]).copy()
        own[i] = False
        oth = labels != labels[i]
        s_own = G[i, own].sum() / max(np.sqrt(G[np.ix_(own, own)].sum()), 1e-12)
        s_oth = G[i, oth].sum() / max(np.sqrt(G[np.ix_(oth, oth)].sum()), 1e-12)
        vals.append(s_own - s_oth)
    return float(np.mean(vals))


def ag1_max_null(grams: dict, recs: list[dict], n_perm: int, seed: int) -> dict:
    """AG1: max-over-cells median item silhouette vs max-statistic perm null.

    Same per-item permutation reused across cells within a draw (frozen).
    Also returns the anaphora-class null at the best cell (CONFOUNDED input).
    """
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    cells = sorted(grams.keys())
    keys = sorted(next(iter(grams.values())).keys())
    ana_keys = [k for k in keys if k[0] == "ana"]

    obs_med = {}
    obs_item = {}
    for c in cells:
        sils = {k: sil_from_gram(*grams[c][k]) for k in keys}
        obs_item[c] = sils
        obs_med[c] = float(np.median(list(sils.values())))
    best_cell = max(obs_med, key=obs_med.get)
    obs_max = obs_med[best_cell]
    non_ana = [k for k in keys if k[0] != "ana"]
    obs_ana = (float(np.median([obs_item[best_cell][k] for k in ana_keys]))
               if ana_keys else 0.0)
    obs_gap = (float(np.median([obs_item[best_cell][k] for k in non_ana]) - obs_ana)
               if ana_keys else 0.0)

    null_max = np.empty(n_perm)
    null_gap = np.empty(n_perm)
    for p in range(n_perm):
        perms = {k: rng.permutation(len(grams[cells[0]][k][1])) for k in keys}
        meds = {}
        for c in cells:
            sils = {k: sil_from_gram(grams[c][k][0], grams[c][k][1][perms[k]])
                    for k in keys}
            meds[c] = np.median(list(sils.values()))
            if c == best_cell and ana_keys:
                null_gap[p] = (np.median([sils[k] for k in non_ana])
                               - np.median([sils[k] for k in ana_keys]))
        null_max[p] = max(meds.values())
    p_max = float(np.mean(null_max >= obs_max))
    p_gap = float(np.mean(null_gap >= obs_gap)) if ana_keys else 1.0
    return {
        "best_cell": best_cell, "obs_max_median_sil": obs_max, "p": p_max,
        "floor": AG1_FLOOR, "pass": bool(p_max < ALPHA and obs_max >= AG1_FLOOR),
        "per_cell_median": obs_med, "per_item_best_cell": {
            f"{k[0]}-{k[1]:02d}": v for k, v in obs_item[best_cell].items()},
        "ana_median_best_cell": obs_ana, "canary_gap": obs_gap, "gap_p": p_gap,
        "null_max_q95": float(np.quantile(null_max, 0.95)),
    }


def _cell_matrix(data: dict, cell: str) -> np.ndarray:
    reg, ls = cell.split(":L")
    return data[reg][int(ls)].astype(np.float64)


def _pole_axis(X: np.ndarray, labels: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    return X[labels == 0].mean(axis=0) - X[labels == 1].mean(axis=0)


def _loio_acc(X_items: list[np.ndarray], lab_items: list[np.ndarray]) -> float:
    """Leave-one-item-out pole classification (median-centered sign rule)."""
    axes = [_pole_axis(X, lab) for X, lab in zip(X_items, lab_items, strict=True)]
    total, correct = 0, 0
    n = len(X_items)
    for i in range(n):
        axis = np.mean([axes[j] for j in range(n) if j != i], axis=0)
        proj = X_items[i] @ axis
        pred = (proj - np.median(proj) < 0).astype(int)  # D1 projects positive
        correct += int((pred == lab_items[i]).sum())
        total += len(lab_items[i])
    return correct / max(total, 1)


def ag2_loio(data: dict, recs: list[dict], cell: str, n_perm: int, seed: int) -> dict:
    """AG2 at the AG1 cell: LOIO class-axis transfer, perm null on accuracy."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed + 1)
    X = _cell_matrix(data, cell)
    per_class = {}
    accs_obs = []
    null = np.zeros(n_perm)
    for cls in CLASSES:
        keys = sorted({r["item"] for r in recs if r["cls"] == cls})
        rows = {i: [r["idx"] for r in recs if r["cls"] == cls and r["item"] == i]
                for i in keys}
        Xi = [X[rows[i]] for i in keys]
        Li = [np.array([recs[j]["pole"] for j in rows[i]]) for i in keys]
        acc = _loio_acc(Xi, Li)
        per_class[cls] = acc
        accs_obs.append(acc)
        for p in range(n_perm):
            Lp = [rng.permutation(lab) for lab in Li]
            null[p] += _loio_acc(Xi, Lp)
    obs = float(np.mean(accs_obs))
    null /= len(CLASSES)
    pv = float(np.mean(null >= obs))
    return {"cell": cell, "acc": obs, "per_class": per_class, "p": pv,
            "generic": bool(pv < ALPHA and obs > 0.5)}


def ag3_lofo(data: dict, recs: list[dict], cell: str, n_perm: int, seed: int) -> dict:
    """AG3 advisory at the AG1 cell: leave-one-frame-out transfer."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed + 2)
    X = _cell_matrix(data, cell)

    def lofo_acc(labels_by_idx: dict[int, int]) -> float:
        total, correct = 0, 0
        for cls in CLASSES:
            crecs = [r for r in recs if r["cls"] == cls]
            for f in range(N_FRAMES):
                train = [r["idx"] for r in crecs if r["frame"] != f]
                test = [r["idx"] for r in crecs if r["frame"] == f]
                lt = np.array([labels_by_idx[i] for i in train])
                axis = _pole_axis(X[train], lt)
                proj = X[test] @ axis
                pred = (proj - np.median(proj) < 0).astype(int)
                lab = np.array([labels_by_idx[i] for i in test])
                correct += int((pred == lab).sum())
                total += len(test)
        return correct / max(total, 1)

    true_lab = {r["idx"]: r["pole"] for r in recs}
    obs = lofo_acc(true_lab)
    null = np.empty(n_perm)
    keys = sorted({(r["cls"], r["item"]) for r in recs})
    rows = {k: [r["idx"] for r in recs if (r["cls"], r["item"]) == k] for k in keys}
    for p in range(n_perm):
        lab = dict(true_lab)
        for k in keys:
            idxs = rows[k]
            vals = [true_lab[i] for i in idxs]
            for i, v in zip(idxs, rng.permutation(vals), strict=True):
                lab[i] = int(v)
        null[p] = lofo_acc(lab)
    pv = float(np.mean(null >= obs))
    return {"cell": cell, "acc": obs, "p": pv, "pass": bool(pv < ALPHA and obs > 0.5)}


def decide(g: dict) -> str:
    if not g["ag0"]["pass"]:
        return "VOID"
    if not g["ag1"]["pass"]:
        return "NO-GEOMETRY"
    if g["confounded_style"]["fires"]:
        return "CONFOUNDED-STYLE"
    return "SEPARABLE-GENERIC" if g["ag2"]["generic"] else "SEPARABLE-LOCAL"


def analyze(data: dict, recs: list[dict], n_perm: int, seed: int,
            det: dict | None) -> dict:
    """Full frozen gate tree. data = {register: {layer: X}} (CMR'd)."""
    bstats = battery_stats(recs)
    det = det or {"sign_flip_frac": 0.0, "value_rel_dev": 0.0, "planted": True}
    ag0 = {
        **bstats, **det,
        "det_ok": bool(det["sign_flip_frac"] < DET_SIGN_TOL
                       and det["value_rel_dev"] < DET_VALUE_TOL),
    }
    ag0["pass"] = bool(ag0["len_ok"] and ag0["det_ok"])

    grams = item_grams(data, recs)
    ag1 = ag1_max_null(grams, recs, n_perm=n_perm, seed=seed)
    cell = ag1["best_cell"]
    ag2 = ag2_loio(data, recs, cell, n_perm=max(200, n_perm // 5), seed=seed)
    ag3 = ag3_lofo(data, recs, cell, n_perm=200, seed=seed)
    conf = {"ana_median": ag1["ana_median_best_cell"], "canary_gap": ag1["canary_gap"],
            "gap_p": ag1["gap_p"], "ag3_pass": ag3["pass"],
            "fires": bool(ag1["pass"]
                          and ag1["ana_median_best_cell"] < AG1_FLOOR
                          and ag1["gap_p"] < ALPHA)}
    g = {"ag0": ag0, "ag1": ag1, "ag2": ag2, "ag3": ag3, "confounded_style": conf}
    g["verdict"] = decide(g)
    return g


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Planted worlds (--validate; real battery + real analysis path — s331 law)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

PLANT_D = 96
PLANT_LAYERS = list(range(6))
PLANT_CELL = ("route", 3)
PLANT_S = 4.0


def _plant(world: str, seed: int) -> tuple[dict, list[dict]]:
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    recs = build_battery(smoke=False)
    n = len(recs)

    def u() -> np.ndarray:
        v = rng.normal(size=PLANT_D)
        return v / np.linalg.norm(v)

    axes_cls = {c: u() for c in CLASSES}
    axes_item = {(r["cls"], r["item"]): None for r in recs}
    axes_item = {k: u() for k in axes_item}
    axes_pole_style = {(c, pole): u() for c in ("scope", "att") for pole in (0, 1)}
    axes_frame_shared = {(c, f): u() for c in CLASSES for f in range(N_FRAMES)}

    data = {reg: {li: rng.normal(size=(n, PLANT_D)) for li in PLANT_LAYERS}
            for reg in ("route", "value")}
    reg, li = PLANT_CELL
    X = data[reg][li]
    for r in recs:
        sgn = 1.0 if r["pole"] == 0 else -1.0
        if world == "generic":
            X[r["idx"]] += PLANT_S * sgn * axes_cls[r["cls"]]
        elif world == "local":
            X[r["idx"]] += PLANT_S * sgn * axes_item[(r["cls"], r["item"])]
        elif world == "style":
            # cue-style world: pole-level style axes exist only where pole frame
            # sets differ (scope/att); the anaphora canary (pole-shared frames)
            # carries frame style but NO pole-separating component
            if r["cls"] == "ana":
                X[r["idx"]] += PLANT_S * axes_frame_shared[(r["cls"], r["frame"])]
            else:
                X[r["idx"]] += PLANT_S * axes_pole_style[(r["cls"], r["pole"])]
        elif world == "nogeom":
            pass
        else:
            raise ValueError(world)
    data = {reg: {li: cmr(M) for li, M in by.items()} for reg, by in data.items()}
    return data, recs


def run_validate(n_perm: int, seed: int) -> int:
    want = {
        "generic": "SEPARABLE-GENERIC",
        "local": "SEPARABLE-LOCAL",
        "nogeom": "NO-GEOMETRY",
        "style": "CONFOUNDED-STYLE",
    }
    recs = build_battery(smoke=False)
    bs = battery_stats(recs)
    log(f"[ag] battery: {bs['n_prompts']} prompts / {bs['n_items']} items | "
        f"median pole len delta {bs['median_pole_len_delta_words']:.2f} words "
        f"(tol {LEN_TOL_WORDS}) {'OK' if bs['len_ok'] else 'FAIL'}")
    ok = bs["len_ok"]
    for world, expect in want.items():
        data, recs = _plant(world, seed=42)
        g = analyze(data, recs, n_perm=n_perm, seed=seed, det=None)
        hit = g["verdict"] == expect
        ok &= hit
        log(f"[ag] world={world!r}: verdict={g['verdict']} (want {expect}) "
            f"{'OK' if hit else 'FAIL'} | AG1 {g['ag1']['obs_max_median_sil']:.3f} "
            f"p={g['ag1']['p']:.3f} cell={g['ag1']['best_cell']} | "
            f"AG2 acc={g['ag2']['acc']:.3f} p={g['ag2']['p']:.3f} | "
            f"AG3 acc={g['ag3']['acc']:.3f} p={g['ag3']['p']:.3f} | "
            f"ana_med={g['ag1']['ana_median_best_cell']:.3f} "
            f"gap_p={g['ag1']['gap_p']:.3f}")
    log(f"[ag] {'ALL PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}")
    return 0 if ok else 1


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Real collection (both registers, per-layer, last token)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def collect_both(model, tokenizer, device, prompts, max_length, want_layers):
    """Returns (gate {li: (N,d_ff)}, hid {li: (N,d_model)}, plen (N,))."""
    import torch

    gate_mods = find_gate_modules(model)
    n_layers = len(gate_mods)
    want = set(want_layers)
    buf: dict[int, np.ndarray] = {}

    def mk_hook(li):
        def hook(_m, _inp, out):
            buf[li] = out[0, -1].detach().float().cpu().numpy().astype(np.float32)
        return hook

    handles = [mod.register_forward_hook(mk_hook(li))
               for (li, _nm, mod) in gate_mods if li in want]
    gate = {li: [] for li in want_layers}
    hid = {li: [] for li in want_layers}
    plen = []
    try:
        with torch.no_grad():
            for i, p in enumerate(prompts):
                enc = tokenizer(p, return_tensors="pt", truncation=True,
                                max_length=max_length).to(device)
                out = model(**enc, output_hidden_states=True)
                for li in want_layers:
                    gate[li].append(buf[li])
                    h = out.hidden_states[li + 1][0, -1]
                    hid[li].append(h.detach().float().cpu().numpy().astype(np.float32))
                plen.append(int(enc["input_ids"].shape[1]))
                if (i + 1) % 50 == 0:
                    log(f"[ag] collected {i + 1}/{len(prompts)}")
    finally:
        for hd in handles:
            hd.remove()
    return ({li: np.stack(v) for li, v in gate.items()},
            {li: np.stack(v) for li, v in hid.items()},
            np.array(plen, dtype=np.int32), n_layers)


def _json_native(o):
    if isinstance(o, np.bool_):
        return bool(o)
    if isinstance(o, np.integer):
        return int(o)
    if isinstance(o, np.floating):
        return float(o)
    if isinstance(o, np.ndarray):
        return o.tolist()
    raise TypeError(f"Object of type {o.__class__.__name__} is not JSON serializable")


def run_real(args) -> int:
    import torch
    from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer

    recs = build_battery(smoke=args.smoke)
    prompts = [r["prompt"] for r in recs]
    out = Path(args.out or f"results/p_ambiguity_gate_s337/"
                           f"{'smoke_4b' if args.smoke else 'run_14b'}")
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    dtype = {"float32": torch.float32, "float16": torch.float16,
             "bfloat16": torch.bfloat16}[args.dtype]
    log(f"[ag] loading {args.model_id} ({args.dtype}, {args.device})")
    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(args.model_id)
    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(args.model_id, torch_dtype=dtype)
    model.to(args.device).eval()

    n_layers_probe = len(find_gate_modules(model))
    want_layers = pick_layers(n_layers_probe)
    log(f"[ag] {n_layers_probe} layers -> capture {want_layers}")

    # det-repeat: first prompt appended again; compared then dropped
    gate, hid, plen, _ = collect_both(model, tok, args.device,
                                      [*prompts, prompts[0]], args.max_length,
                                      want_layers)
    flips, rdevs = [], []
    for li in want_layers:
        a, b = np.sign(gate[li][0]), np.sign(gate[li][-1])
        flips.append(float(np.mean(a != b)))
        ha, hb = hid[li][0], hid[li][-1]
        rdevs.append(float(np.linalg.norm(ha - hb) / max(np.linalg.norm(ha), 1e-9)))
        gate[li], hid[li] = gate[li][:-1], hid[li][:-1]
    plen = plen[:-1]
    det = {"sign_flip_frac": float(np.max(flips)),
           "value_rel_dev": float(np.max(rdevs)), "planted": False}
    log(f"[ag] det-repeat: sign_flip {det['sign_flip_frac']:.4f} "
        f"value_rel {det['value_rel_dev']:.4f}")

    data = {
        "route": {li: cmr(np.sign(gate[li]).astype(np.float64)) for li in want_layers},
        "value": {li: cmr(hid[li].astype(np.float64)) for li in want_layers},
    }
    if args.device == "mps":
        del model
        gc.collect()
        torch.mps.empty_cache()

    g = analyze(data, recs, n_perm=args.n_perm, seed=args.seed, det=det)
    log(f"[ag] VERDICT: {g['verdict']} | AG1 {g['ag1']['obs_max_median_sil']:.4f} "
        f"p={g['ag1']['p']:.4f} cell={g['ag1']['best_cell']} | "
        f"AG2 acc={g['ag2']['acc']:.3f} p={g['ag2']['p']:.4f} | "
        f"ana_med={g['ag1']['ana_median_best_cell']:.3f} "
        f"gap_p={g['ag1']['gap_p']:.3f}")

    with (out / "results.jsonl").open("w") as fh:
        for r, pl in zip(recs, plen, strict=True):
            fh.write(json.dumps({**r, "plen": int(pl)}, default=_json_native) + "\n")
    (out / "gates.json").write_text(json.dumps(g, indent=2, default=_json_native))
    np.savez_compressed(out / "route_signs.npz",
                        **{f"L{li}": np.sign(gate[li]).astype(np.int8)
                           for li in want_layers})
    np.savez_compressed(out / "value_hidden.npz",
                        **{f"L{li}": hid[li].astype(np.float16) for li in want_layers})
    meta = {
        "run_id": out.name, "probe": PROBE, "frozen": FROZEN,
        "pre_data_instantiations": {
            "ag1_floor": AG1_FLOOR, "alpha": ALPHA, "len_tol_words": LEN_TOL_WORDS,
            "det_tols": [DET_SIGN_TOL, DET_VALUE_TOL], "n_perm": args.n_perm,
            "masses": {"SEPARABLE-GENERIC": 25, "SEPARABLE-LOCAL": 30,
                       "NO-GEOMETRY": 25, "CONFOUNDED-STYLE": 15, "VOID": 5},
        },
        "timestamp_utc": datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(),
        "model_id": args.model_id, "device": args.device, "dtype": args.dtype,
        "seed": args.seed, "smoke": bool(args.smoke),
        "n_variants": len(recs), "battery_hash": battery_hash(recs),
        "git_sha": git_sha(), "python": platform.python_version(),
        "platform": platform.platform(),
        "lib_versions": {"torch": torch.__version__,
                         "numpy": np.__version__},
        "gates": g,
    }
    (out / "meta.json").write_text(json.dumps(meta, indent=2, default=_json_native))
    log(f"[ag] wrote {out}/")
    return 0


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    ap.add_argument("--model-id", default="Qwen/Qwen3-14B")
    ap.add_argument("--device", default="mps")
    ap.add_argument("--dtype", default="bfloat16",
                    choices=["float32", "float16", "bfloat16"])
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0)
    ap.add_argument("--n-perm", type=int, default=1000)
    ap.add_argument("--max-length", type=int, default=64)
    ap.add_argument("--out", default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--validate", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--smoke", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    if args.validate:
        return run_validate(n_perm=min(args.n_perm, 300), seed=args.seed)
    return run_real(args)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

Within-prompt: both candidate answers sit in the SAME prompt, same forward

Substrate: the s335 matched triples (`build_variants` via `build_battery`,
18 triples / 54 variants, 9 kernel-certified clean flips), identical layout

  A  capture live    - correct NF discards `e`, naive NF is built from it
  B  binders renamed - capture-free, NF head = cap var  => ground truth: not-e
  P  head var swapped- capture-free, NF head = `e`      => ground truth: e

Readout: value-weighted attention (s206 scar: never bare QK) from the answer

instantiation; per-layer stored for the RC4 depth advisory).

Frozen statistics (knowledge page section P-CONE-ROUTING):

  primary   rho_e   = (mass_A(e) - mass_B(e)) / (mass_P(e) - mass_B(e))
  secondary rho_Sel = same shape on Sel = mass(cap) - mass(e), within-prompt.
            Named bound: A carries the cap token TWICE (binder + argument);
            mass is read at the ARGUMENT position, binder mass is diagnostic.

Gate tree (frozen): RC0 sanity -> RC1 CALIBRATION make-or-break read FIRST
(mass_P(e) > mass_B(e) paired p<0.05 AND Cliff's delta >= 0.2, corroborated by
Sel_B > Sel_P) -> RC2 primary (bootstrap CI on median rho_e must exclude 0.5)
-> RC3 secondary sign agreement -> RC4 depth advisory. Nulls: placebo `f`
(must not discriminate), shuffled-variant-label (== the sign-flip permutation),
distance control (B/P are geometry-identical with opposite answers - the pole
contrast IS the distance control).

Verdicts: VOID / NO-CALIBRATION / NAIVE-ROUTING / CORRECT-ROUTING /
UNDIFFERENTIATED. The 3 advisory read-mass records from
results/p_prefill_cone_s335/run_14b (cap_000) are DISCLOSED and excluded -
this is a fresh run directory; nothing is read from that run.

Standing bound: attention mass is correlational (s206) - a positive licenses
"reads from", not "uses".
